name: How sweet?
question: Sweetness compared with table sugar (sugar = 1). Each gridline step is ten times sweeter.

items.name: Lactose (milk sugar)
items.fact: Milk sugar is only about a sixth as sweet as table sugar.

items.name: Maltose (malt sugar)
items.fact: Maltose forms when starch is broken down, as in brewing.

items.name: Sorbitol
items.fact: Sorbitol is common in sugar-free chewing gum.

items.name: Glucose
items.fact: Glucose is the sugar your blood carries around your body.

items.name: Table sugar (sucrose)
items.fact: Sucrose is the yardstick: everything else is measured against it.

items.name: Fructose (fruit sugar)
items.fact: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar.

items.name: Cyclamate
items.fact: Cyclamate was discovered in 1937 by a student who noticed his cigarette tasted sweet.

items.name: Stevia
items.fact: Stevia sweeteners come from the leaves of a South American plant.

items.name: Aspartame
items.fact: Aspartame was discovered by accident when a chemist licked his finger.

items.name: Saccharin
items.fact: Saccharin, from 1879, is the oldest artificial sweetener.

items.name: Sucralose
items.fact: Sucralose is made from sugar by swapping three parts of the molecule for chlorine.

items.name: Monellin (berry protein)
items.fact: Monellin is a sweet protein from a West African berry.

items.name: Thaumatin
items.fact: Thaumatin comes from the katemfe fruit of West Africa.

items.name: Neotame
items.fact: Neotame is a close relative of aspartame, about 40 times sweeter.

items.name: Lugduname
items.fact: Lugduname is one of the sweetest substances known; it has never been approved as food.
